category: Heat Transfer Module: Interfaces, Multiphysics Couplings and Studies
description: Heat Transfer Module (COMSOL 6.4) physics interfaces beyond the basic solid/fluid ones (solids and fluids, local thermal nonequilibrium, packed beds, moist porous media, building materials, moist air, films, fractures, orbital loads, absorbing-scattering media, radiative beam, moisture transport family), the heat-related multiphysics couplings, preset studies and general modeling settings. Java type strings are taken from the COMSOL 6.4 Application Library model files (.mph/.java).

tools.name: Heat Transfer in Solids and Fluids (ht)
tools.description: Version of the Heat Transfer interface that is added automatically by the Conjugate Heat Transfer multiphysics interfaces: a Solid model is active on all domains and a Fluid model is added but not active until you give it a selection. It solves conduction, convection and radiation with the same settings as Heat Transfer in Fluids, so a first-order (linear) temperature discretization is the default. Use it whenever solid and fluid domains are coupled in one temperature field, typically together with a Laminar or Turbulent Flow interface and the Nonisothermal Flow coupling.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Heat Transfer in Solids and Fluids (or added by Conjugate Heat Transfer > Laminar/Turbulent Flow). Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("ht", "HeatTransferInSolidsAndFluids", "geom1")

parameters.name: Solid (solid1) / Fluid (fluid1)
parameters.description: Default domain nodes (SolidHeatTransferModel, FluidHeatTransferModel); assign fluid domains to fluid1.

parameters.name: Physical Model > Reference temperature Tref
parameters.description: Used for the reference enthalpy and the reference density of incompressible nonisothermal flow (variable ht.Tref).

parameters.name: Discretization > Temperature
parameters.description: Linear by default (like Heat Transfer in Fluids); set via prop("ShapeProperty").set("order_temperature", ...).

tools.notes: Identical to the physics created by the Conjugate Heat Transfer branch; Nonisothermal Flow interfaces differ only in having Fluid as the default domain node. The same tag 'ht' is used by all Heat Transfer interface versions.

tools.name: Local Thermal Nonequilibrium (ht, porous media interface)
tools.description: Porous-media version of the Heat Transfer interface in which a Porous Medium node is active on all domains with Porous medium type = Local thermal nonequilibrium, so separate fluid temperature Tf and solid temperature Ts are solved and coupled by an interstitial transfer term proportional to Ts - Tf. Use it for fast transients, high-conductivity contrast, metal foams or packed beds where the phases are not in thermal equilibrium. A Local Thermal Nonequilibrium Boundary node marks the two-temperature boundaries; phase-specific conditions are added under the Fluid and Porous Matrix subnodes.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Porous Media > Local Thermal Nonequilibrium. Java (equivalent setting on a porous node): model.component("comp1").physics("ht").feature("porous1").set("PorousMediumType", "LocalThermalNonequilibrium")

parameters.name: Porous medium type
parameters.description: LocalThermalEquilibrium, LocalThermalNonequilibrium or Packed bed.

parameters.name: Interstitial heat transfer coefficient / specific surface area
parameters.description: Define the fluid-solid exchange term q_sf = h_sf a_sf (Ts - Tf).

parameters.name: Fluid / Porous Matrix subnodes
parameters.description: Initial Values, Thermal Insulation, Continuity (fluid only), and optional heat sources, fluxes or phase change per phase.

tools.notes: If Ts - Tf is negligible use Heat Transfer in Porous Media (local equilibrium) instead - it is cheaper. Theory: 'Local Thermal Nonequilibrium' and 'When Should Local Thermal Equilibrium and Nonequilibrium Be Considered?' in the Heat Transfer Module User's Guide.

tools.name: Heat Transfer in Packed Beds (ht)
tools.description: Porous-media interface whose default Porous Medium node uses Porous medium type = Packed bed: the macroscale fluid temperature equation is coupled to a microscale equation for the radial temperature inside spherical pellets, instead of a single volume-averaged solid temperature. Use it for catalytic reactors, regenerators and thermal storage beds when pellet conductivity is low enough that intra-pellet gradients matter. Pellets and Pellet-Fluid Interface subnodes define pellet properties and the coupling (heat transfer coefficient or temperature continuity).
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Porous Media > Heat Transfer in Packed Beds; domain node Porous Medium > Pellets (type PelletsPorousMediumHeatTransferModel) and Pellet-Fluid Interface (PelletFluidInterfacePorousMediumHeatTransferModel).

parameters.name: Pellets: radius, porosity, k, rho, Cp
parameters.description: Pellet size distribution and material properties used by the microscale equation.

parameters.name: Pellet-Fluid Interface
parameters.description: Coupling by a film heat transfer coefficient or by continuity of fluid and pellet surface temperature.

parameters.name: Heat Source (Pellets)
parameters.description: Volumetric source inside pellets, e.g. reaction heat.

tools.example:
Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Porous Media > Heat Transfer in Packed Beds
Porous Medium 1 > Pellets 1: pellet radius 2[mm], k = 0.5[W/(m*K)]
Porous Medium 1 > Pellet-Fluid Interface 1: heat transfer coefficient from correlation
Fluid subnode: velocity from Brinkman Equations (br)
tools.notes: Radiation effects are only handled on the outer surface of the pellets. Related: Chemical_Reaction_Engineering_Module packed_bed_reactor_3d uses the Pellets functionality with chemistry.

tools.name: Heat Transfer in Moist Porous Media (ht)
tools.description: Heat Transfer interface version added by the Moist Porous Media version of the Heat and Moisture Transport multiphysics interface; a Moist Porous Medium node is active on all domains. It solves a convection-diffusion temperature equation with properties averaged over the solid matrix, liquid water and moist air, assuming local thermal equilibrium between the phases. Evaporation heat and the enthalpy carried by liquid and vapor fluxes are supplied by the Heat and Moisture coupling.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Heat and Moisture Transport > Moist Porous Media (adds ht + mt + Heat and Moisture coupling). Domain node Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("mporous1", "MoistPorousMediumHeatTransferModel", 2)

parameters.name: Moist Porous Medium > Porous Matrix / Liquid Water / Moist Air subnodes
parameters.description: Matrix conductivity and heat capacity, liquid and gas Darcy velocities (from a flow interface or user defined).

parameters.name: Effective conductivity model
parameters.description: Averaging of the phase conductivities for the effective thermal conductivity.

parameters.name: Discretization
parameters.description: Linear temperature shape functions by default.

tools.notes: In the library the potato and steam drying models create it under an HeatTransferInMoistAir interface; any ht version can host a Moist Porous Medium node. Pair with Equilibrium or Nonequilibrium Moisture Transport in Porous Media.

tools.name: Heat Transfer in Building Materials (ht)
tools.description: Heat Transfer interface added by the Building Materials version of Heat and Moisture Transport; a Building Material node is active by default. The temperature equation is a diffusion equation with effective properties of the dry matrix plus moisture and a latent-heat term Lv div(delta_p grad(phi_w p_sat)) for vapor diffusion, following the building-physics (EN 15026-type) formulation. It uses second-order temperature elements by default and is meant for walls, roofs and insulation assemblies.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Heat and Moisture Transport > Building Materials. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("ht", "HeatTransferInBuildingMaterials", "geom1")

parameters.name: Building Material (bm1)
parameters.description: Dry density, heat capacity, effective thermal conductivity k_eff(w), vapor permeability delta_p, latent heat Lv (type BuildingMaterialHeatTransferModel).

parameters.name: Model inputs
parameters.description: Relative humidity (from mt) and absolute pressure.

parameters.name: Building material library
parameters.description: Materials from the Building library (concrete, pine, gypsum board, glass wool, vapor barriers...) supply hygrothermal properties.

tools.notes: Use Ambient Properties with ASHRAE meteorological data for realistic exterior climate. The coupling adds the latent heat source; do not add it twice.

tools.name: Heat Transfer in Moist Air (ht)
tools.description: Heat Transfer interface added by the Moist Air version of Heat and Moisture Transport (and by the Heat and Moisture Flow interfaces): a Moist Air node is active on all domains and rho, Cp and k are functions of the vapor content. It models convection and diffusion in humid air, e.g. evaporative cooling, condensation in enclosures and HVAC; first-order temperature discretization as for fluids.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Heat and Moisture Transport > Moist Air. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("ht", "HeatTransferInMoistAir", "geom1")

parameters.name: Moist Air (ma1)
parameters.description: Input quantity: relative humidity, vapor concentration, moisture content or vapor mass fraction; velocity field (type MoistAirHeatTransferModel).

parameters.name: Absolute pressure
parameters.description: From the flow interface or minput.pA (1 atm default).

parameters.name: Convectively Enhanced Conductivity
parameters.description: Optional subnode replacing a flow solution by Nusselt-enhanced conductivity.

tools.notes: Moist-air variables such as ht.phi, ht.T_dp (dew point), ht.psat and ht.xvap (humidity ratio) become available.

tools.name: Heat Transfer in Films (htlsh)
tools.description: Thin-structure interface (Heat Transfer in Shells family) for conduction, convection and radiation in fluid films represented by boundaries carrying a layered material; the default boundary node is Fluid. Through-thickness temperature variation is resolved with the Extra Dimension product space, or bypassed with Shell type = Nonlayered shell and a user thickness for thermally thin films. Typical uses are lubricating films, thin liquid layers and air gaps.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Thin Structures > Heat Transfer in Films. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("htlsh", "HeatTransferInFilmsLM", "geom1")

parameters.name: Shell type
parameters.description: Layered shell (needs Single Layer Material, Layered Material Link/Stack or Material with Layer thickness) or Nonlayered shell (thickness Lth).

parameters.name: Fluid (default node)
parameters.description: Film velocity, fluid properties, thermally thin or general layer model.

parameters.name: Thermal Insulation (edge), Initial Values
parameters.description: Other default nodes.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics().create("htlsh", "HeatTransferInFilmsLM", "geom1");
// Application Library: Rotordynamics_Module/Tutorials/rotor_thermal_stress (oil film between rotor and bearing)
tools.notes: Shares tag htlsh and settings with Heat Transfer in Shells; use a Thermal Connection multiphysics coupling to connect it to a domain heat transfer interface.

tools.name: Heat Transfer in Fractures (htlsh)
tools.description: Thin-structure interface for heat transfer in fractures (thin porous layers) represented by boundaries with a layered material; its default node is Porous Medium and the equation uses porous-media averaged properties with local thermal equilibrium. Through-thickness temperature variation can be resolved via the extra dimension or lumped with a nonlayered shell. Use it for rock fractures, thin porous gaskets or filters embedded in a 3D model.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Thin Structures > Heat Transfer in Fractures (tag htlsh). The equivalent node inside a domain Heat Transfer interface is Fracture (type PorousMediumLayeredShell).

parameters.name: Porous Medium (default)
parameters.description: Fracture porosity, matrix and fluid properties, fluid velocity (e.g. from Fracture Flow).

parameters.name: Shell type
parameters.description: Layered shell or Nonlayered shell with thickness Lth.

parameters.name: Thermal Insulation (edge), Initial Values
parameters.description: Default edge condition and initial temperature.

tools.example:
Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Thin Structures > Heat Transfer in Fractures
Materials > Single Layer Material: thickness 1[mm], porosity 0.3
Porous Medium 1 > Fluid: velocity from Fracture Flow (Subsurface Flow Module)
tools.notes: Type string for the stand-alone interface is not used in any 6.4 Application Library model; the domain-level Fracture node is used in Subsurface_Flow_Module/Heat_Transfer/geothermal_doublet.

tools.name: Orbital Thermal Loads (otl)
tools.description: Radiation interface (Heat Transfer > Radiation) that computes radiative loads on spacecraft: direct solar flux, planet albedo and planet infrared emission plus surface-to-surface radiation between spacecraft parts, using the radiosity method like the Surface-to-Surface Radiation interface. It holds the orbit, attitude, planet and Sun definitions and an Events Timeline for maneuvers and eclipses. Supported in 3D with Time Dependent, Orbit Calculation, Orbit Thermal Loads and Orbital Temperature studies.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Radiation > Orbital Thermal Loads. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("otl", "OrbitalThermalLoadsEvents", "geom1")

parameters.name: Radiation settings
parameters.description: Same as S2S (wavelength dependence, hemicube/ray shooting); refractive index forced to 1.

parameters.name: Default global nodes
parameters.description: Orbital Parameters (op1), Planet Properties (plp1), Sun Properties (sup1), Spacecraft Axes (sa1), Spacecraft Orientation (so1), Events Timeline (et1).

parameters.name: Diffuse Surface (dsurf)
parameters.description: Solar absorptivity/IR emissivity per spectral band for spacecraft surfaces.

tools.notes: Global variables such as otl.R_planet, otl.T_orbit, otl.isIlluminated and otl.Gext1 are available. Generate Events Interface is obsolete since 6.2 - use Events Timeline.

tools.name: Radiation in Absorbing-Scattering Media (rasm)
tools.description: Radiation interface for semitransparent media that absorb and scatter but do not emit (nonemitting), e.g. light diffusion in tissue, turbid liquids or UV reactors. The radiative transfer equation without emission term is solved with the P1 approximation or the discrete ordinates method, and the absorbed power kappa*G becomes a heat source when coupled to heat transfer. Default nodes are Absorbing-Scattering Medium and Opaque Surface (plus Continuity on Interior Boundary with DOM).
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Radiation > Radiation in Absorbing-Scattering Media (rasm); coupled version: Heat Transfer with Radiation in Absorbing-Scattering Media (coupling htrasm1).

parameters.name: Wavelength dependence of radiative properties
parameters.description: Constant (gray), Solar and ambient, or Multiple spectral bands.

parameters.name: Radiation discretization method
parameters.description: Discrete ordinates method (S_N/T_N quadrature sets) or P1 approximation.

parameters.name: Absorbing-Scattering Medium
parameters.description: Absorption coefficient kappa, scattering coefficient sigma_s, scattering phase function.

tools.example:
Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Radiation > Heat Transfer with Radiation in Absorbing-Scattering Media
rasm > Participating Media Settings: Radiation discretization method = Discrete ordinates method, S4
Absorbing-Scattering Medium 1: kappa = 10[1/m], sigma_s = 100[1/m], isotropic phase function
Incident Intensity on the illuminated boundary
tools.notes: Use Radiation in Participating Media when the medium also emits (hot gases, glass melts). The stand-alone interface type string is not used in the 6.4 Application Library models.

tools.name: Radiative Beam in Absorbing Media (rbam)
tools.description: Radiation interface that attenuates collimated incident beams (lasers, focused light) inside a semitransparent material with the Beer-Lambert law; the deposited energy acts as a volumetric heat source when coupled to heat transfer. It is much cheaper than full radiative transfer when scattering and emission are negligible. Default nodes are Absorbing Medium, Transparent Surface and Initial Values; beams are defined with Incident Intensity nodes.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Radiation > Radiative Beam in Absorbing Media (rbam); coupled: Heat Transfer with Radiative Beam in Absorbing Media (coupling htrbam1).

parameters.name: Absorbing Medium
parameters.description: Absorption coefficient kappa of the medium.

parameters.name: Incident Intensity
parameters.description: Beam orientation e and profile: built-in Gaussian (P0, origin O, sigma) or top-hat disk (radius R), or user-defined I0.

parameters.name: Discretization > Intensity
parameters.description: Linear by default; streamline/crosswind stabilization enabled.

tools.example:
Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Radiation > Heat Transfer with Radiative Beam in Absorbing Media
Absorbing Medium 1: kappa = 50[1/m] (glass at 1064 nm)
Incident Intensity 1: e = (0,0,-1), Gaussian, P0 = 20[W], sigma = 0.5[mm]
Study: Time Dependent
tools.notes: For opaque absorbing boundaries use Opaque Surface (rbam); for beams heating only a surface use Deposited Beam Power in Heat Transfer instead.

tools.name: Equilibrium Moisture Transport in Porous Media (mt)
tools.description: Moisture Transport interface for porous media filled with moist air and liquid water in which vapor and liquid are in equilibrium: a Hygroscopic Porous Medium node with the Equilibrium formulation solves one convection-diffusion equation for the total moisture content, linking relative humidity and liquid saturation through a sorption isotherm (moisture storage function). Transport includes vapor diffusion/convection and liquid convection plus capillary flow.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Moisture Transport > Equilibrium Moisture Transport in Porous Media (tag mt). Domain node Java: model.component("comp1").physics("mt").create("hporous1", "HygroscopicPorousMediumModel", 2)

parameters.name: Hygroscopic Porous Medium > Equilibrium between liquid and gas phases
parameters.description: Equilibrium formulation.

parameters.name: Moisture storage function w(phi_w)
parameters.description: Sorption isotherm defining liquid saturation.

parameters.name: Liquid Water / Moist Air / Porous Matrix subnodes
parameters.description: Capillary diffusivity or relative permeability, vapor diffusion, porosity.

tools.example:
Model Wizard > Moisture Transport > Equilibrium Moisture Transport in Porous Media
Hygroscopic Porous Medium 1: porosity 0.4, moisture storage function from material
Moisture Flux on the exposed surface: convective, beta = 1e-3[m/s]
Application Library: Heat_Transfer_Module/Phase_Change/potato_drying
tools.notes: Evaporation source is stored in mt.G_evap for use by a Moisture Flow coupling. If phase nonequilibrium matters use the Nonequilibrium interface.

tools.name: Nonequilibrium Moisture Transport in Porous Media (mt)
tools.description: Moisture Transport interface for porous media where vapor and liquid water are not in equilibrium: separate mass conservation equations for moist air (relative humidity phi_w) and liquid water (saturation s_l) are coupled by an evaporation/condensation term proportional to the difference between partial and equilibrium vapor pressure. A Nonequilibrium Boundary node marks boundaries where both variables are solved. Use it for fast drying, high-temperature processes or strongly wet media.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Moisture Transport > Nonequilibrium Moisture Transport in Porous Media (tag mt); Hygroscopic Porous Medium with Equilibrium between liquid and gas phases = Nonequilibrium formulation.

parameters.name: Evaporation rate factor
parameters.description: Controls the phase-change source term between liquid and vapor.

parameters.name: Liquid Water subnode
parameters.description: Liquid saturation-dependent transport (relative permeability, capillary pressure model).

parameters.name: Moist Air subnode
parameters.description: Vapor diffusion coefficient, gas velocity, relative gas permeability.

tools.example:
Model Wizard > Moisture Transport > Nonequilibrium Moisture Transport in Porous Media
Hygroscopic Porous Medium 1 > Liquid Water: capillary pressure model = van Genuchten
Nonequilibrium Boundary (default) on porous boundaries; apply conditions under the Moist Air / Liquid Water subnodes
tools.notes: Boundary conditions at interface level do not apply on Nonequilibrium Boundary selections; add phase-specific subnodes instead.

tools.name: Moisture Transport in Building Materials (mt)
tools.description: Moisture Transport interface for building envelopes that accounts for moisture storage, capillary liquid transport and vapor diffusion by solving for relative humidity with a Building Material node. It uses quadratic Lagrange elements for relative humidity and is normally coupled to Heat Transfer in Building Materials through the Heat and Moisture coupling. Typical studies are drying of construction moisture, interstitial condensation and seasonal moisture accumulation.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Moisture Transport > Moisture Transport in Building Materials. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("mt", "MoistureTransportInBuildingMaterials", "geom1")

parameters.name: Building Material (bm1)
parameters.description: Moisture storage capacity xi, vapor permeability delta_p, moisture diffusivity D_w.

parameters.name: Moisture Flux / Moisture Content
parameters.description: Exterior conditions (convective moisture flux with ambient humidity).

parameters.name: Thin Moisture Barrier
parameters.description: Vapor barrier on interior boundaries.

tools.notes: Material data from the Building material library (Heat Transfer Module). The equation is designed for building materials; use it carefully for other porous media.

tools.name: Moisture Transport in Free and Porous Media (mt)
tools.description: Moisture Transport interface for models with both open air regions and hygroscopic porous domains: a Moist Air node (all domains) and a Hygroscopic Porous Medium node (empty selection, Nonequilibrium formulation) are added by default. Porous Interface, Free-Porous Interface and Porous-Porous Interface nodes manage flux continuity and optional evaporation at the interfaces. Use it for drying of food or wood in an air stream.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Moisture Transport > Moisture Transport in Free and Porous Media. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("mt", "MoistureTransportFreePorousMedia", "geom1")

parameters.name: Moist Air (ma1)
parameters.description: Vapor diffusion and convection in the air domains.

parameters.name: Hygroscopic Porous Medium (hporous1)
parameters.description: Assign porous domains; choose equilibrium or nonequilibrium formulation.

parameters.name: Free-Porous Interface
parameters.description: Phase change at the interface: no evaporation, or evaporation with a rate factor.

tools.notes: Combine with Free and Porous Media Flow or Laminar Flow + Brinkman and the Moisture Flow coupling for a full drying model.

tools.name: Moisture Transport in Solids (mts)
tools.description: Moisture Transport interface (tag mts) for moisture in the pores of solid porous materials that also accounts for moist-air pressure changes: it solves the total moisture conservation (vapor and liquid at saturation equilibrium) plus an equation for dry-air transport. Its default nodes are Porous Medium, No Flux and Initial Values, and it is used together with Solid Mechanics for hygroscopic swelling.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Moisture Transport > Moisture Transport in Solids. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("mts", "MoistureTransportInSolids", "geom1")

parameters.name: Porous Medium > Porous Matrix / Liquid Water / Moist Air
parameters.description: Porosity, permeability, sorption and diffusion properties.

parameters.name: Moisture Content and Pressure
parameters.description: Boundary condition fixing moisture content and moist-air pressure.

parameters.name: No Flux
parameters.description: Default boundary condition.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics().create("mts", "MoistureTransportInSolids", "geom1");
// Application Library: Structural_Mechanics_Module/Hygroscopic_Swelling/paperboard_roll (also Porous_Media_Flow_Module)
tools.notes: Different tag (mts) from the other Moisture Transport interfaces (mt).

tools.name: Heat Transfer with Surface-to-Surface Radiation (multiphysics coupling, htrad)
tools.description: Boundary multiphysics coupling between a Heat Transfer interface (temperature) and a Surface-to-Surface Radiation interface (radiosity) for radiation in transparent media: it adds the radiative heat source epsilon*(G - e_b(T)) on the radiating side of boundaries and passes T to the radiosity equation. In 1D/2D it disables out-of-plane features of the coupled heat interface because view factors assume an infinite out-of-plane extent. Added automatically by the Heat Transfer with Surface-to-Surface Radiation predefined interface.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Heat Transfer with Surface-to-Surface Radiation (default name htrad1). Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("htrad1", "HeatTransferWithSurfaceToSurfaceRadiation", 1)

parameters.name: Heat transfer / Surface-to-surface radiation
parameters.description: Coupled interfaces (Heat_physics, Rad_physics).

parameters.name: Default domain opacities
parameters.description: From heat transfer (solids opaque, fluids transparent) or controlled by Opacity nodes.

parameters.name: Radiation shield temperatures
parameters.description: Uses the outermost shield temperature when a Radiation Shield is present.

tools.notes: Replaces the older 'Surface-to-surface radiation' checkbox workflow. For radiation to a non-reflecting environment only, the cheaper Surface-to-Ambient Radiation boundary condition is enough.

tools.name: Heat Transfer with Radiation in Participating Media (multiphysics coupling, htrpm)
tools.description: Domain coupling between a Heat Transfer interface and a Radiation in Participating Media interface for conduction, convection and radiation in emitting, absorbing and scattering semitransparent media. It adds the volumetric radiative source Q = kappa*(G - 4*pi*I_b(T)) to the heat equation and the net radiative flux on opaque boundaries, and passes the temperature to the radiative transfer equation (DOM or P1).
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Radiation > Heat Transfer with Radiation in Participating Media, or Multiphysics > Heat Transfer with Radiation in Participating Media (htrpm1). Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("htrpm1", "HeatTransferWithRadiationInParticipatingMedia", 3)

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Heat transfer interface and Radiation in Participating Media interface.

parameters.name: Radiation discretization method
parameters.description: Set on the rpm interface: Discrete ordinates or P1 approximation.

parameters.name: Refractive index n_r
parameters.description: Used in I_b = n_r^2 sigma T^4 / pi.

tools.notes: For optically thick media, the Rosseland approximation (Optically Thick Participating Medium node in ht) avoids solving for intensities.

tools.name: Heat Transfer with Radiation in Absorbing-Scattering Media (multiphysics coupling, htrasm)
tools.description: Domain coupling between Heat Transfer and Radiation in Absorbing-Scattering Media: the incident radiation G absorbed by a nonemitting medium becomes a heat source kappa*G in the heat equation. Use it for light diffusion heating (biological tissue under illumination, UV curing, photothermal processes) where thermal emission of the medium is negligible.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Radiation > Heat Transfer with Radiation in Absorbing-Scattering Media; Multiphysics node default name htrasm1.

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Heat transfer (temperature) and Radiation in Absorbing-Scattering Media (intensity or G).

parameters.name: Wavelength dependence
parameters.description: Gray or banded properties defined on the rasm interface.

tools.example:
Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Radiation > Heat Transfer with Radiation in Absorbing-Scattering Media
rasm: P1 approximation; Absorbing-Scattering Medium: kappa, sigma_s
Incident Intensity on the illuminated surface; Study: Stationary or Time Dependent
tools.notes: Stationary, time-dependent and frequency-domain (thermal perturbation) studies are supported in 3D, 2D and 2D axisymmetry.

tools.name: Heat Transfer with Radiative Beam in Absorbing Media (multiphysics coupling, htrbam)
tools.description: Domain coupling that adds the power deposited by Beer-Lambert attenuated beams (Radiative Beam in Absorbing Media) as a volumetric heat source in a Heat Transfer in Solids interface, and passes temperature back for temperature-dependent absorption. The predefined interface adds ht, rbam and the coupling; it is the standard way to model laser heating inside semitransparent glass, crystals or polymers.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Radiation > Heat Transfer with Radiative Beam in Absorbing Media; Multiphysics node default name htrbam1.

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Heat transfer and Radiative Beam in Absorbing Media.

parameters.name: Beam definition
parameters.description: Incident Intensity nodes in rbam (Gaussian or top-hat, power P0, orientation).

tools.example:
Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Radiation > Heat Transfer with Radiative Beam in Absorbing Media
rbam > Absorbing Medium: kappa = 100[1/m]; Incident Intensity: Gaussian, P0 = 5[W]
ht > Heat Flux (convective) on outer surfaces; Study: Time Dependent 0-10 s
tools.notes: Out-of-plane heat features are disabled in 2D when the coupling is active (infinite medium assumption).

tools.name: Heat Transfer with Orbital Thermal Loads (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined 3D multiphysics interface combining Heat Transfer in Solids and Orbital Thermal Loads with a Heat Transfer with Surface-to-Surface Radiation coupling, so spacecraft temperatures respond to solar, albedo and planet IR loads along the orbit together with internal radiation exchange. Supports Time Dependent, Orbit Calculation, Orbital Temperature and Orbit Thermal Loads studies.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Radiation > Heat Transfer with Orbital Thermal Loads (adds ht, otl and htrad1).

parameters.name: Heat Transfer in Solids
parameters.description: Conduction, thin layers (MLI, panels), heat sources for electronics.

parameters.name: Orbital Thermal Loads
parameters.description: Orbit, attitude, Sun and planet definitions.

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Orbital Temperature (orbitlist in fractions of an orbit) for periodic temperature cycles.

tools.notes: Heat sources of instruments can be switched with the Events interface (explicit events) as in spacecraft_thermal_analysis.

tools.name: Nonisothermal Flow (multiphysics coupling, nitf)
tools.description: Domain coupling between a Fluid Flow interface and a Heat Transfer interface for flows whose density and viscosity depend on temperature: it feeds velocity and absolute pressure to the heat interface, temperature and density to the flow, synchronizes the reference temperature and turbulence settings, and adds pressure work and viscous dissipation. It also provides thermal wall functions and turbulent Prandtl number models (Kays-Crawford etc.) for RANS flows. Supports low-Mach flows (Ma < 0.3); used by Conjugate Heat Transfer and Nonisothermal Flow predefined interfaces.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Nonisothermal Flow (nitf1). Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("nitf1", "NonIsothermalFlow", 3)

parameters.name: Specify density
parameters.description: From the fluid flow interface, custom linearized density (Boussinesq-like) or from heat transfer; BoussinesqApproximation checkbox.

parameters.name: Thermal turbulence model
parameters.description: Turbulent Prandtl number model (Kays-Crawford default) or user Prt; thermal wall function.

parameters.name: Include viscous dissipation / irreversible losses
parameters.description: Energy balance options (includeViscousDissipation).

parameters.name: Reference temperature
parameters.description: From the heat transfer interface or the fluid flow interface.

tools.notes: Overrides any Pressure Work or Viscous Dissipation subnodes in the heat interface. See also the Stationary/Time Dependent One-Way NITF preset studies.

tools.name: Heat and Moisture (multiphysics coupling, ham)
tools.description: Domain coupling between Heat Transfer and Moisture Transport for building materials, moist air or moist porous media: it passes temperature to the moisture equation (saturation conditions, temperature-dependent transport) and moisture content to the heat equation (moisture-dependent properties), and adds latent heat of evaporation plus the diffusive enthalpy flux of vapor. Latent heat sources on Wet Surface / Moist Surface boundaries are included when 'Include latent heat source on surfaces' is selected.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Heat and Moisture (ham1). Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("ham1", "HeatAndMoisture", 2)

parameters.name: Heat transfer / Moisture transport
parameters.description: Coupled interfaces (Heat_physics, Moist_physics).

parameters.name: includeLatentHeatSourceOnSurfaces
parameters.description: Adds L_v * g_evap on Wet Surface and Moist Surface boundaries.

tools.notes: Requires matching domain models in both interfaces (Building Material + Building Material, Moist Air + Moist Air, or Moist Porous Medium + Hygroscopic Porous Medium).

tools.name: Heat and Moisture Transport (multiphysics interfaces: Moist Air, Moist Porous Media, Building Materials)
tools.description: Predefined multiphysics interfaces under Heat Transfer > Heat and Moisture Transport that each add a heat interface version, a Moisture Transport interface and the Heat and Moisture coupling: Moist Air (Heat Transfer in Moist Air + Moisture Transport in Air), Moist Porous Media (Heat Transfer in Moist Porous Media + Equilibrium Moisture Transport in Porous Media) and Building Materials (Heat Transfer in Building Materials + Moisture Transport in Building Materials). Latent heat sources and the diffusive enthalpy flux are handled automatically.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Heat and Moisture Transport > Moist Air | Moist Porous Media | Building Materials

parameters.name: Moist Air version
parameters.description: Condensation/evaporation in air-filled enclosures, evaporative cooling.

parameters.name: Moist Porous Media version
parameters.description: Drying of food, wood, soils with liquid water and vapor in pores.

parameters.name: Building Materials version
parameters.description: Hygrothermal performance of walls and roofs (building-physics formulation).

tools.example:
Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Heat and Moisture Transport > Building Materials
Materials: Building library > Wood, pine; Gypsum board; Vapor barrier
Definitions > Ambient Properties: Meteorological data (ASHRAE 2021)
Study: Time Dependent over one year
Application Library: Heat_Transfer_Module/Buildings_and_Constructions/wood_frame_wall
tools.notes: Stationary, time-dependent and thermal perturbation frequency-domain studies are supported in all dimensions.

tools.name: Moisture Flow (multiphysics coupling, mf)
tools.description: Domain coupling between a Fluid Flow interface and a Moisture Transport interface for flows of moist air whose density and viscosity depend on moisture content; it passes the velocity/pressure to moisture transport and the moist-air properties (and, in porous media, porosity reduced by liquid saturation and relative gas permeability) to the flow. It also synchronizes turbulence (turbulent Schmidt number, Kays-Crawford) and complements Wall, Screen and Interior Fan features with moisture effects.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Moisture Flow (mf1). Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("mf1", "MoistureFlow", 2)

parameters.name: Fluid flow / Moisture transport
parameters.description: Coupled interfaces (Fluid_physics, Transport_physics).

parameters.name: Turbulent mass transfer model
parameters.description: Kays-Crawford or user-defined turbulent Schmidt number ScT (0.71 default).

parameters.name: Account for Stefan velocity at walls
parameters.description: Adds the evaporation-induced wall velocity.

tools.notes: Low Mach number flows (Ma < 0.3). The Moisture Flow predefined interfaces (Laminar, Turbulent, Porous Media Flow) add this coupling automatically.

tools.name: Heat and Moisture Flow (multiphysics interfaces)
tools.description: Predefined multiphysics interfaces that model coupled heat, moisture and airflow: the Laminar/Turbulent versions add Single-Phase Flow, Heat Transfer in Moist Air and Moisture Transport in Air, while the Brinkman Equations version adds Brinkman Equations, Heat Transfer in Moist Porous Media and Equilibrium Moisture Transport in Porous Media. All include the Moisture Flow, Heat and Moisture and Nonisothermal Flow couplings. Use them for drying ovens, condensation in electronics enclosures and humid ventilation.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Heat and Moisture Transport > Heat and Moisture Flow > Laminar Flow | Turbulent Flow (Algebraic yPlus, L-VEL, k-eps, SST, Low Re k-eps) | Porous Media Flow

parameters.name: Preset studies
parameters.description: Stationary/Time Dependent (fully coupled), one-way NITF and one-way MF variants solving the flow first.

parameters.name: Couplings
parameters.description: mf1 (Moisture Flow), ham1 (Heat and Moisture), nitf1 (Nonisothermal Flow).

tools.example:
Model Wizard > Heat and Moisture Flow > Turbulent Flow, k-epsilon
Inlet: humid air phi = 0.8, T = 30 degC
Wet Surface on product surfaces (mt), Heat Flux on walls (ht)
Study: Stationary, one-way NITF
Related Application Library model with the same couplings (mf1, ham1): Heat_Transfer_Module/Power_Electronics_and_Electronic_Cooling/condensation_electronic_device_transport_diffusion
tools.notes: Turbulence variants listed in the Heat Transfer Module interface guide: Algebraic yPlus, L-VEL, k-eps, SST and Low Re k-eps; more are available with the CFD Module.

tools.name: Marangoni Effect (multiphysics coupling, mar)
tools.description: Boundary coupling between a Laminar Flow and a Heat Transfer interface that adds thermocapillary (Marangoni) shear stress on a fluid-fluid interface when surface tension depends on temperature, plus normal curvature forces. Important in welding pools, crystal growth and electron-beam melting. The surface tension coefficient can be user defined or taken from a library of liquid-gas pairs.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Marangoni Effect (mar1). Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("mar1", "Marangoni", 1)

parameters.name: Surface tension coefficient sigma
parameters.description: User defined (e.g. sigma0 + gamma*(T - T0)) or library pair (WaterAir, ...).

parameters.name: Contact angle
parameters.description: Specified directly or from surface energies.

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Fluid_physics (spf) and Heat_physics (ht).

tools.notes: Formulation intended for laminar flow regimes only.

tools.name: Electromagnetic Heating, Layered Shell (multiphysics coupling, ehls)
tools.description: Boundary coupling that uses electromagnetic surface losses from a shell electromagnetic interface (e.g. Electric Currents in Layered Shells) as a heat source in a Heat Transfer in Shells interface for layered materials represented by boundaries. Individual layers can be selected so Joule heating is deposited only in the conductive plies. Typical for printed heaters, laminated busbars and heated windshields.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Electromagnetic Heating, Layered Shell. Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("ehls1", "ElectromagneticHeatingLayeredShell", 2)

parameters.name: Restrict to layered boundaries
parameters.description: Apply only where a layered material is defined.

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Electromagnetic interface (electric potential) and Heat Transfer interface (temperature).

parameters.name: Shell properties > Use all layers
parameters.description: Clear to select individual layers of a Layered Material Link/Stack.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("ehls1", "ElectromagneticHeatingLayeredShell", 2);
// Application Library: Composite_Materials_Module/Multiphysics/heating_circuit_layered
tools.notes: Requires Composite Materials Module or AC/DC Module functionality for layered electric currents. For domain problems use the Electromagnetic Heating coupling (emh).

tools.name: Thermoelectric Effect, Layered Shell (multiphysics coupling)
tools.description: Boundary coupling that adds the Peltier heat flux q = P_s*J to the Heat Transfer in Shells equation and the Seebeck current density -sigma_s*S_s*grad_t(T) to the shell electric current density, for thermoelectric layers represented by boundaries. It is the layered-shell counterpart of the Thermoelectric Effect domain coupling (tee).
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Thermoelectric Effect, Layered Shell (select boundaries with a layered material; couple the electromagnetic and heat transfer interfaces).

parameters.name: Boundary selection / Restrict to layered boundaries
parameters.description: Boundaries carrying the thermoelectric layers.

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Electric potential interface and Heat Transfer in Shells interface.

parameters.name: Seebeck coefficient S, Peltier coefficient P = S*T
parameters.description: Taken from the layer materials (e.g. Bi2Te3 from the Thermoelectric material library).

tools.example:
Model: thin-film thermoelectric generator on a substrate
Materials > Layered Material: Bi2Te3 layer 50 um (Thermoelectric library)
Physics: Electric Currents in Layered Shells + Heat Transfer in Shells
Multiphysics > Thermoelectric Effect, Layered Shell on the film boundaries
tools.notes: For bulk thermoelectric legs use multiphysics().create("tee1", "ThermoelectricEffect", 3) (Verification_Examples/thermoelectric_leg).

tools.name: Thermal Expansion, Layered and Thin Layer (multiphysics couplings)
tools.description: Couplings that add thermal strain from a shell temperature field to structural models of layered or thin structures and account for the mechanical losses in the heat balance: Thermal Expansion, Layered couples Heat Transfer in Shells with Layered Shell, and Thermal Expansion, Thin Layer couples a Thin Layer (heat) with a Thin Layer in Solid Mechanics. Use them for warpage of laminates, coatings and PCB traces.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Thermal Expansion, Layered (Java type ThermalExpansionLS) or Thermal Expansion, Thin Layer (ThermalExpansionTL). Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("tel1", "ThermalExpansionLS", 2); multiphysics().create("tetl1", "ThermalExpansionTL", 2)

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Heat transfer (shell or domain with thin layer) and the structural shell/thin-layer interface.

parameters.name: Thermal expansion properties
parameters.description: Coefficient of thermal expansion and strain reference temperature from the layer materials.

tools.notes: Details of Thermal Expansion, Layered are in the Structural Mechanics Module User's Guide.

tools.name: Thermal Connection, Layered Shell, Surfaces and Edges (multiphysics couplings)
tools.description: Global/boundary couplings that enforce temperature continuity between a domain Heat Transfer interface and a Heat Transfer in Shells interface with Shell type = Layered shell. The Surfaces variant connects shared or facing surfaces (assemblies), the Edges variant connects a shell edge to the adjacent domain surface, with options to connect all layers or selected layers. Use them to attach laminated heat spreaders or fins modeled as shells to solid parts.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Thermal Connection, Layered Shell, Surfaces | Edges. Java (edges): model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("tcls1", "ThermalConnectionLayeredShellEdges", 1)

parameters.name: Connection type
parameters.description: Shared boundaries (default) or Facing boundaries (with tolerance).

parameters.name: Manual control of selections
parameters.description: Edit edge/boundary selections instead of the automatic ones.

parameters.name: Constraint settings
parameters.description: Pointwise or weak constraints.

tools.notes: For shells with Shell type = Nonlayered shell use Thermal Connection, Nonlayered Shell.

tools.name: Thermal Connection, Nonlayered Shell (multiphysics coupling)
tools.description: Coupling that defines temperature continuity between a domain Heat Transfer interface and a Heat Transfer in Shells interface whose Shell type is Nonlayered shell (lumped through-thickness temperature). Connection types are Edges (shell edge to domain surface), Shared boundaries (default) and Facing boundaries.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Thermal Connection, Nonlayered Shell (select the Heat transfer and Heat transfer in shells interfaces).

parameters.name: Connection type
parameters.description: Edges, Shared boundaries, or Facing boundaries.

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Any domain heat transfer interface and any shell heat transfer interface.

tools.example:
Model: aluminium fin array modeled as shells on a solid heat-sink base
Physics: Heat Transfer in Solids (base) + Heat Transfer in Shells (fins, Nonlayered shell, Lth = 1[mm])
Multiphysics > Thermal Connection, Nonlayered Shell: Connection type = Edges
tools.notes: Cheaper than meshing thin fins; accuracy depends on the thin-layer assumption.

tools.name: Laser, Induction and Microwave Heating (Heat Transfer Module predefined multiphysics)
tools.description: Electromagnetic Heating branch entries listed in the Heat Transfer Module: Laser Heating (Electromagnetic Waves, Beam Envelopes + Heat Transfer in Solids, Wave Optics Module), Induction Heating (Magnetic Fields + Heat Transfer in Solids, AC/DC Module) and Microwave Heating (Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain + Heat Transfer in Solids, RF Module). In each, the Electromagnetic Heating coupling (emh) passes EM losses as a heat source and temperature back to temperature-dependent EM properties, assuming the EM cycle is short compared with thermal time scales.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Electromagnetic Heating > Laser Heating | Induction Heating | Microwave Heating. Coupling Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("emh1", "ElectromagneticHeating", 3)

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Frequency-Transient (induction), Frequency-Stationary or Frequency-Transient (microwave/laser).

parameters.name: Electromagnetic Heating coupling
parameters.description: Domain and boundary loss contributions; temperature to EM material properties.

tools.notes: Joule Heating (Electric Currents + ht) is included with the Heat Transfer Module; the other three require the respective EM module licenses.

tools.name: Thermal Perturbation, Frequency Domain and Eigenfrequency (heat transfer studies)
tools.description: Preset studies of the Heat Transfer interfaces for harmonic heat transfer: the temperature is decomposed as T = T0 + Re(T' e^{j omega t}) around an equilibrium T0 (from a previous stationary step), and the linearized problem is solved in the frequency domain for sinusoidal heat loads, which is far cheaper than a long transient. Thermal Perturbation, Eigenfrequency computes thermal eigenmodes (decay rates). Harmonic loads are defined with Harmonic Perturbation subnodes or the harmonicPerturbation option of sources.
tools.usage: Add Study > Preset Studies for Selected Physics > Thermal Perturbation, Frequency Domain (or Eigenfrequency); the sequence contains a Stationary step followed by a Frequency-Domain Perturbation step.

parameters.name: Frequencies
parameters.description: List of excitation frequencies f in the Frequency-Domain Perturbation step.

parameters.name: Harmonic Perturbation subnode
parameters.description: Temperature perturbation Delta T0 added to a prescribed temperature.

parameters.name: Heat Source / Boundary Heat Source harmonic perturbation
parameters.description: Mark a source as harmonic perturbation (harmonicPerturbation = 1).

tools.example:
Model: periodic surface heating of a coated substrate
Heat Transfer in Solids: Boundary Heat Source with harmonic perturbation amplitude 1e4[W/m^2]
Study: Thermal Perturbation, Frequency Domain -> Stationary step (T0) + Frequency-Domain Perturbation step, f = 10^range(-1,0.1,2) Hz
Results: abs(T) and arg(T) of the perturbation versus frequency
tools.notes: Valid only if temperature changes are small or properties are constant (linearization). Supported by ht and htlsh interfaces and the heat-related multiphysics interfaces.

tools.name: Stationary and Time Dependent, One-Way NITF (conjugate heat transfer studies)
tools.description: Preset studies of the Nonisothermal Flow and Conjugate Heat Transfer interfaces that solve the flow variables first and the heat transfer variables in a second step (one-way coupling), either stationary or time dependent. They are much faster and more robust when buoyancy and temperature-dependent flow properties are negligible, e.g. forced-convection electronics cooling. For natural convection or strong property variation use the fully coupled Stationary/Time Dependent (with Initialization) studies.
tools.usage: Add Study > Preset Studies for Selected Multiphysics > Stationary, One-Way NITF | Time Dependent, One-Way NITF

parameters.name: Step 1
parameters.description: Fluid flow (with wall distance initialization for turbulence models).

parameters.name: Step 2
parameters.description: Heat transfer using the stored velocity field.

tools.example:
Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Conjugate Heat Transfer > Turbulent Flow, k-epsilon
Study: Stationary, One-Way NITF (step 1: Wall Distance Initialization + flow; step 2: heat transfer)
Typical case: forced-air cooling of a heat sink where buoyancy is negligible
tools.notes: Moisture analogues (one-way MF) exist for the Heat and Moisture Flow interfaces.

tools.name: Orbit Calculation, Orbit Thermal Loads and Orbital Temperature (studies)
tools.description: Study steps for the Orbital Thermal Loads interface: Orbit Calculation computes the spacecraft trajectory, attitude and eclipse events for visualization; Orbit Thermal Loads computes solar, albedo and planet IR loads and radiosity at the positions in orbitlist (in fractions of an orbit); Orbital Temperature solves the transient spacecraft temperature over several orbits. Combining Orbit Thermal Loads and Orbital Temperature in one study gives periodic temperature cycles.
tools.usage: Java: model.study("std1").create("oc", "OrbitCalculation"); model.study("std1").create("otl", "OrbitThermalLoads"); model.study("std1").create("ot", "OrbitalTemperature")

parameters.name: orbitlist
parameters.description: Orbit positions/times as fractions of the orbital period, e.g. range(0,0.02,1).

parameters.name: plotgrouparr
parameters.description: Default plots to generate.

tools.notes: Only 3D components. Fast tumbling approximation in the Events Timeline averages solar loads and skips external view factors.

tools.name: Ambient Properties (Heat Transfer Module, ASHRAE meteorological data)
tools.description: Component Definitions node that defines ambient temperature, absolute pressure, relative humidity, wind velocity, precipitation rate and clear-sky solar irradiances for use as inputs in Heat Flux, Temperature, Initial Values, Diffuse Surface, External Radiation Source and Moisture Transport features. Ambient data can be user defined or interpolated from ASHRAE 2013/2017/2021 meteorological data of more than 8000 weather stations worldwide, averaged monthly and hourly over several years.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Ambient Properties, or right-click Component > Definitions > Ambient Properties. Java: model.component("comp1").common().create("ampr1", "AmbientProperties")

parameters.name: AmbientData
parameters.description: User defined, MeteorologicalData2013/2017/2021 (ASHRAE).

parameters.name: Location / Weather station
parameters.description: From list, around a location (lat/long), or station ID.

parameters.name: Time / Ambient conditions
parameters.description: Date and local time (Update time from solver for transient runs); Average, Low, High, Lowest, Highest, user deviation or correction conditions for temperature, dew point, wind speed and precipitation; optional Filter diurnal variation.

parameters.name: Variables
parameters.description: ampr1.T_amb, ampr1.p_amb, ampr1.phi_amb, ampr1.v_amb (plus solar irradiance variables).

tools.notes: External Radiation Source with Solar position can take its location from an Ambient Properties node that uses ASHRAE data.

tools.name: Heat Part Library (parameterized heat sinks)
tools.description: Part library shipped with the Heat Transfer Module containing fully parameterized heat sink geometries composed of a rectangular base and arrays of pins or straight fins: Heat Sink - Parameterized Fin Types (fin_type 1, 2 or 3 editable), Heat Sink - Pin Fins, Heat Sink - Dissimilar Border Pins and Heat Sink - Straight Fins. Fillets, chamfers and notches can be applied to the fins, parameter checks validate inputs, and fins can be built as solids or boundaries (for thin-layer modeling).
tools.usage: Geometry toolbar > Parts > Part Libraries > Heat Transfer Module > (heat sink part) > Add to Geometry; set Input Parameters in the resulting Part Instance node.

parameters.name: fin_type
parameters.description: 1 pin fins, 2 dissimilar border pins, 3 straight fins (Parameterized Fin Types part).

parameters.name: Number, dimensions and placement of fins
parameters.description: Counts in x/y, fin height, thickness, spacing, base size.

parameters.name: Fins as boundaries
parameters.description: Build fins as surfaces for use with Thin Layer or shells.

tools.example:
Geometry 1 > Parts > Part Libraries > Heat Transfer Module > Heat Sink - Straight Fins
Part Instance: adjust the number of fins, fin height and base dimensions in Input Parameters
Then: Heat Transfer in Solids and Fluids + Laminar/Turbulent Flow (Conjugate Heat Transfer) around the sink
tools.notes: Parts are geometry subsequences (GeomSubsequenceCallFeature PartInstance) and can be swept in parametric studies.

tools.name: Physical Model and Out-of-Plane Settings (Heat Transfer interface)
tools.description: Interface-level settings of every Heat Transfer interface: in 2D and 1D axisymmetric the out-of-plane Thickness dz (default 1 m), in 1D the cross-sectional area Ac and perimeter Pc, and the Reference temperature Tref used for the reference enthalpy and for incompressible nonisothermal flow density. When a radiation coupling is active, dz/Ac are forced to unit length because view factors assume an infinite out-of-plane extent. Physical model checkboxes also enable isothermal domains, surface-to-surface radiation and porous-media features in the interface.
tools.usage: Component > Heat Transfer (ht) > Settings > Physical Model. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").prop("PhysicalModelProperty").set("dz", "d"); prop("PhysicalModelProperty").set("Tref", "T0")

parameters.name: dz
parameters.description: Out-of-plane thickness in 2D (PhysicalModelProperty).

parameters.name: Tref
parameters.description: Reference temperature (variable ht.Tref).

parameters.name: order_temperature
parameters.description: Temperature shape order (ShapeProperty): 1 for fluids by default, 2 for solids.

tools.notes: Out-of-Plane Heat Flux / Radiation nodes add losses through the out-of-plane faces of a 2D or 1D model.

tools.name: Consistent and Inconsistent Stabilization (Heat Transfer interfaces)
tools.description: Numerical stabilization options for convection-dominated heat transfer (fluids, translational motion, porous flow). Consistent stabilization - streamline diffusion and crosswind diffusion, both on by default, with an optional dynamic subgrid time scale - vanishes as the solution converges and does not alter the model. Inconsistent isotropic diffusion (tuning parameter delta_id) adds artificial diffusion and should be used only as a last resort.
tools.usage: Model Builder > Show More Options > Stabilization; then ht > Consistent Stabilization / Inconsistent Stabilization. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").prop("ConsistentStabilization").set("heatCrosswindDiffusion", "0")

parameters.name: heatStreamlineDiffusion
parameters.description: Streamline diffusion (default on).

parameters.name: heatCrosswindDiffusion
parameters.description: Crosswind diffusion for sharp gradients (default on).

parameters.name: useDynamicSubgridTimescaleHT
parameters.description: Estimate temporal variation instead of solver time step.

parameters.name: HeatIsotropicDiffusion / delidht
parameters.description: Inconsistent isotropic diffusion and its tuning parameter (0.25 default).

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("ht").prop("ConsistentStabilization").set("heatCrosswindDiffusion", "0");
// used in Application Library models where crosswind diffusion smears thin thermal boundary layers
tools.notes: Linear sources written as Linear source (q_s*T) in Heat Source are accounted for in streamline diffusion.

tools.name: Solver Guidelines for Heat Transfer and Radiation Problems
tools.description: Heat Transfer Module guidance on solver configuration: the temperature equation is linear only for constant properties without radiation, otherwise Newton iterations are required; direct solvers suit small/2D models while iterative (AMG) solvers are default for large 3D models; time-dependent steps benefit from consistent initialization and controlled time steps. Dedicated guidelines cover surface-to-surface radiation (segregated radiosity step, hemicube resolution) and radiation in participating media (DOM with reduced Jacobian, segregated intensities, inconsistent stabilization).
tools.usage: Study > Solver Configurations > Solution > Stationary/Time-Dependent Solver > Fully Coupled or Segregated; see 'Solver Settings' chapter of the Heat Transfer Module User's Guide.

parameters.name: Linear solver
parameters.description: Direct (MUMPS/PARDISO) or iterative GMRES/CG with multigrid.

parameters.name: Nonlinear solver
parameters.description: Newton damping, Jacobian update, tolerance factor.

parameters.name: Radiation groups / segregated steps
parameters.description: Speed up S2S and DOM problems.

tools.example:
Study 1 > Solver Configurations > Solution 1 > Stationary Solver 1 > Segregated 1
Segregated Step 1: T; Segregated Step 2: rad.J (radiosity)
Iterative 1: GMRES with Multigrid (AMG) for large 3D conjugate heat transfer
tools.notes: Heat Transfer Module User's Guide sections 'Linearity Property of the Temperature Equation', 'Guidelines for Solving Surface-to-Surface Radiation Problems' and '... Radiation in Participating Media ...'.

tools.name: Bulk Temperature Evaluation (Heat Transfer)
tools.description: Procedure for evaluating the bulk (mixing-cup) temperature T_b = integral(rho Cp T u.tau)/integral(rho Cp u.tau) over a pipe cross section, used to compute wall heat transfer coefficients h = q_w/(T_w - T_b). In 3D the diskint(R, expr, tol) operator integrates over a disk perpendicular to an edge along the pipe axis (with a General Extrusion to access the tangent), and in 2D a line integral over the cross section is used.
tools.usage: Results > Derived Values or Component Couplings; expression example on an axis edge: diskint(R, ht.rho*ht.Cp*T*(u*genext1(t1x)+v*genext1(t1y)+w*genext1(t1z)), 1e-3)/diskint(R, ht.rho*ht.Cp*(...), 1e-3)

parameters.name: R
parameters.description: Disk radius large enough to cover the tube cross section.

parameters.name: tol
parameters.description: Numerical tolerance of diskint.

parameters.name: dom test
parameters.description: Multiply by (dom==n) to restrict to the fluid domain.

tools.example:
Definitions > General Extrusion genext1 (edge to domain mapping)
Results > 1D Plot > Line Graph on pipe axis: expression Tb = diskint(D/2, ...)/diskint(D/2, ...)
h_local = ht.ntflux/(T - Tb) on the wall
tools.notes: See 'Evaluating the Bulk Temperature' in the Heat Transfer Module User's Guide; related Verification_Examples/circular_tube_nitf_laminar.

tools.name: Through-Thickness Evaluation in Layered Materials (Heat Transfer in Shells results)
tools.description: Built-in operators and datasets for evaluating temperatures inside layered materials used by Thin Layer, Thin Film, Fracture and Heat Transfer in Shells: xdimTag.atxd1(xd, expr) (2D) or atxd2 (3D) evaluates an expression at through-thickness coordinate xd (0 = downside, th = upside), and per-feature operators such as ht.sls1.xdintopall integrate through the thickness. The Layered Material dataset and Through Thickness plots show layer-wise results.
tools.usage: Results > Datasets > Layered Material; Results > 1D Plot > Through Thickness; expressions like slmat1_xdim.atxd2(0.5*slmat1.th, T) or ht.sls1.xdintopall(T)/slmat1.th

parameters.name: xdimTag
parameters.description: Extra dimension tag, e.g. slmat1_xdim (see Equation View of the thin-layer node).

parameters.name: xd
parameters.description: Coordinate in the extra dimension from 0 to the total thickness (slmat1.th).

parameters.name: Tu / Td
parameters.description: Upside and downside temperatures (ht.Tu, ht.Td) of a thin layer.

tools.notes: ht.sls2.xdintopall is used in Application Library heat models with layered thin layers.

tools.name: Nucleate Pool Boiling Correlation (Rohsenow, Heat Transfer Module)
tools.description: Built-in Rohsenow correlation for the heat flux of nucleate pool boiling on a clean surface immersed in a liquid, available as the Nucleate boiling heat flux option of Heat Flux, Out-of-Plane Heat Flux, Isothermal Domain Interface and as the Nucleate Boiling Heat Rate component of the Lumped Thermal System. Predefined fluids (water, benzene, n-pentane, ethanol) each come with a list of surface materials and finishes (for example polished copper for water, chromium for benzene) that supply C_sf and the Prandtl exponent s; the critical heat flux is also documented.
tools.usage: Heat Flux > Flux type = Nucleate boiling heat flux > Fluid (Water, Benzene, n-Pentane, Ethanol, From material) > Surface.

parameters.name: C_sf, s
parameters.description: Liquid-surface combination factor and Prandtl number exponent.

parameters.name: T_sat, L_v, sigma, p_A
parameters.description: Saturation temperature, latent heat, liquid-vapor surface tension, ambient pressure (From material option).

parameters.name: Validity
parameters.description: Only for T_sat + ~10 K < T < T_sat + ~30 K for water; wrong results below T_sat.

tools.example:
Heat Flux 1 > Flux type: Nucleate boiling heat flux
Fluid: Water, Surface: Copper (polished)
Study: Stationary with an electric heater Heat Source on the plate
tools.notes: Correlation of Rohsenow for pool nucleate boiling; see also 'Critical Heat Flux for Nucleate Boiling'.

tools.name: Equivalent Thermal Conductivity Correlations (enclosed cavities)
tools.description: Nusselt-number correlations used by the Convectively Enhanced Conductivity subnode and by Thermal Connection / Conductive Thermal Resistor with convection enhancement to replace natural convection in closed cavities by an enhanced conductivity k_eq = Nu*k: Horizontal cavity with bottom heating (height H, temperature difference) and Vertical cavity with sidewall heating (height H, plate distance L). This avoids solving a flow field for air gaps in windows, double walls or electronic enclosures.
tools.usage: Fluid > Convectively Enhanced Conductivity > Nusselt number correlation: Horizontal cavity heated from below | Vertical rectangular cavity | User defined

parameters.name: H, L
parameters.description: Cavity height and plate distance.

parameters.name: Delta T
parameters.description: Automatic (max - min exterior boundary temperature) or user defined.

parameters.name: Dynamic viscosity
parameters.description: Needed to evaluate the Rayleigh number (not for moist air).

tools.notes: Only thermally induced density variations are considered in these correlations.
